chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yan said: We asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him)

about a man from the people of Mecca who went out to some of the provinces, then returned and passed by some of the stations that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had designated; is he allowed to perform Tamattu'? He said: 'I do not claim that it is not for him, and the Ihram with Hajj is more beloved to me.'

And I saw someone ask Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and that was on the first night of the month of Ramadan, so he said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I have intended to fast in Medina.' He said: 'You will fast, if Allah wills.'
He said to him: 'And I hope that my departure will be in the ten days of Shawwal.' He said: 'You will depart, if Allah wills.'
He said to him: 'I have intended to perform Hajj on your behalf or on behalf of your father, so what should I do?' He said to him: 'Perform Tamattu'.'

He said to him: 'Indeed, Allah may grant me the favor of visiting the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and visiting you, and peace be upon you, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on your behalf, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of your father, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of some of my brothers or on my own behalf, so what should I do?' He said to him: 'Perform Tamattu'.'
He repeated the same statement to him three times, saying to him: 'I am residing in Mecca and my family is with me there,' and he would say: 'Perform Tamattu'.'
After that, a man from our companions asked him, saying: 'I intend to perform Umrah alone this month,' meaning Shawwal. He said to him: 'You are held hostage by Hajj.'
The man said to him: 'My family and home are in Medina, and I have family and a home in Mecca, and between them are families and homes.' He said: 'You are held hostage by Hajj.'
The man said to him: 'Indeed, I have farms around Mecca and I intend to go out in a state of permissibility (non-Ihram), and when it is time for Hajj, I will perform Hajj.'

As for the resident of Mecca, if he has stayed for less than two years, it is permissible for him to perform Tamattu'. If he has stayed for more than that, his ruling is the ruling of the people of Mecca, that he is not required to perform Tamattu'.
This is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in between)
key_terms.الْإِهْلَالُ بِالْحَجِّ: Ihram with Hajj (entering the state of consecration specifically for Hajj)
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيتُ: Mawaqit (stations/places where pilgrims enter the state of Ihram)
key_terms.الْمُجَاوِرُ: Al-Mujawir (a resident of Mecca who is not a permanent native)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tamattu' Hajj for residents of Mecca based on their duration of stay?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction for Meccan residents (Muqim) performing Tamattu' Hajj, establishing a two-year threshold for residency status. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of intention (niyyah) and the specific ruling that those residing in Mecca for over two years are exempt from the Tamattu' form, mirroring the status of permanent residents. The text further illustrates the practical application of these rules through dialogues with Imam Musa al-Kazim and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq regarding varying travel and residency scenarios.
